scenes.narration: Welcome to IELTS Winners. This is Examiner's Margin, a step-by-step lesson on IELTS Academic Writing Task One. Today, we will learn how to describe a table and build a high-scoring four-paragraph report.
Start with the household expenditure table. It compares four countries: Canada, Japan, Mexico, and Germany. The categories are housing, food, transport, and others.
Look at housing. Canada has the highest figure, at twenty-eight percent. Germany follows at twenty-six percent, Japan at twenty-four percent, and Mexico at twenty percent.
Now compare the other categories. Food accounts for twenty-four percent in Mexico, higher than in the other three countries. Transport varies from ten percent in Japan to fourteen percent in Mexico.

The biggest contrast is in the Others category. Japan records forty-eight percent, Germany forty-five percent, and Mexico forty-two percent, while Canada has just fourteen percent. That contrast is especially useful for your overview.
Our goal is to turn these figures into a clear four-paragraph Task One response, not simply to repeat every number in the table.

In this lesson, you will identify key comparisons, select the most important data, write a four-paragraph Band Eight or Nine sample answer, and use effective vocabulary and connectors. You will also learn a simple shortcut for tackling any table. Let's break it down, step by step.
